prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact needs (system type, home size, budget, timing, warranty preferences). I can help you find the best option for your situation. To start, answer a few quick questions and I’ll pull together vetted local recommendations and a comparison:
- Are you replacing a central AC, heat pump, or window/mini‑split?
- Zip code or neighborhood in Atlanta
- Rough budget or target price range
- Do you have a brand preference (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Goodman, etc.)?
- Do you need financing or want a maintenance plan?

If you want to move forward right now, here are practical steps and checks you can use to choose a high‑quality Atlanta contractor, plus typical price expectations:

What to look for
- Proper licensing & insurance for Georgia contractors.
- NATE‑certified technicians and factory training for the brand they’ll install.
- Positive recent reviews (Google, Yelp) and a good BBB rating.
- Written, itemized estimates from at least 3 companies.
- A proper Manual J load calculation (not just “match the old unit”).
- Detailed scope: equipment model/SEER, ductwork evaluation, permit and disposal, thermostat, labor warranty and manufacturer warranty.
- Clear timeline, start/end dates, and who will do the work (employee techs vs. subcontractors).
- Financing options and available rebates/utility incentives.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are you licensed and insured in Georgia? Can you show proof?
- Do you perform a Manual J load calculation? Can I see it with the estimate?
- Which equipment brands and SEER ratings do you recommend and why?
- What’s included in the installation price (duct sealing, line sets, permit, haul‑away)?
- What are the warranties (parts, labor, extended labor)?
- Are the installers employees? Who supervises the job?
- Do you offer maintenance agreements and priority service?

Typical cost range (Atlanta, general ballpark)
- Replacement of a central AC (including removal and basic duct hookup): roughly $3,500–$10,000 depending on tonnage, SEER, brand, and whether ductwork needs repair or replacement.
- Heat pump replacements are similar in price; minisplits usually cost more per zone.
(These are ballpark figures — get written quotes.)

Red flags
- High‑pressure sales, “today‑only” discounts, or very low bids without detailed scope.
- No written estimate or refusal to do a Manual J load calculation.
- Refusal to provide license/insurance or technician certifications.

If you’d like, give me your zip code and the system type and I’ll find 3–5 well‑rated contractors in your immediate area, with a short pros/cons list for each and a recommended next step. Which would you prefer?
